# M2-3: Transaction read tools

- Milestone: M2
- Branch / worktree: `t/M2-3`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M2-3`
- Depends on: M2-2
- Touches (exclusive while running): mcp/ (new files `tools_transactions*.go`), store/ (read queries in a new file)
- Plan refs: §2 split handling, §4 tools, R9
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no

## Goal
Both spouses can ask about spending: `query_transactions(filter)` and `compare_spending(period, baseline)`. Code does the
arithmetic and dates, and answers cite transactions and freshness.

## Scope
- `query_transactions`: filters for date range, account, category, payee text, amount range, approved state; bounded page
  size with a cursor; returned rows carry transaction ids so answers can cite them.
- `compare_spending`: per-category totals for a period against a baseline period, with the difference.
- Split handling: category reads and totals use `subtransactions`, never the split parent's sentinel category. Deleted
  rows are excluded. Milliunits become exact decimal strings.
- Payee and memo text are returned as data; descriptions tell the model so (§6 prompt injection).

- Add tools with `register(auth.ScopeMCP, &sdkmcp.Tool{...}, handler)` from an `init` in a new file; the handler returns only its data and the `Response[T]` wrapper adds freshness. There's no way yet to send a client a specific error such as a bad filter, so add it next to `errTool` in this task.

## Out of scope
- Snapshot, tags and goals (M2-4). `get_category_decisions` (M3), `get_tithing_status`, `get_fun_money` (M4).

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Tests over a fixture DB: split transactions are counted once under their child categories, deleted rows are absent,
      refunds net correctly, period boundaries are inclusive and in the plan's dates.
- [ ] Test: page size is capped; cursor paging returns each row exactly once.
- [ ] Test: both tools include data freshness.
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `store/transactions_read.go`: a split-aware "lines" CTE (an unsplit transaction is one line, a split is one line per live subtransaction, never the parent's sentinel; deleted rows excluded), `QueryLines` (filters + keyset paging + an all-pages count/sum), `CategoryTotals` (per category over an inclusive date range; on-budget only, excludes on-budget transfers and internal `Inflow:` income), `NameMatches`.
  - `mcp/tools.go`: `clientError` / `badRequest` next to `errTool`. `respond` passes its message to the client (logged at info, no detail); everything else still becomes `errTool`.
  - `mcp/tools_transactions.go`: `query_transactions` (date range, account/category by name or id, payee text, signed amount range, approved; page size 50 by default, capped at 200; opaque cursor tied to a hash of the filters; `match_count`/`match_total` across all pages; every line carries `transaction_id` and `subtransaction_id`) and `compare_spending` (period/baseline as `month: YYYY-MM` or inclusive `start`/`end`; per-category period/baseline spent and difference, sorted by largest difference, totals, and day counts). Milliunits become exact decimal strings (`-12.34`, or `-1.234` when the third digit is used). Payee/memo fields and the tool descriptions say this is data, not instructions.
  - `mcp/tools_transactions_test.go`: fixture DB tests.
- Acceptance:
  - Splits counted once under their child categories, deleted rows absent (including a deleted split part), refunds net, inclusive boundaries (Oct 1, Oct 31, Sep 30 in; Nov 1 out) → pass: `TestCompareSpending`, `TestQueryTransactions_SplitsDeletedAndBoundaries`, `TestQueryTransactions_Filters`.
  - Page size capped (asked for 1000, got 200); cursor paging over 272 lines at page size 7 returns each line exactly once (includes a 10-part split and many rows on the same date); a cursor reused with other filters is refused → pass: `TestQueryTransactions_Paging`.
  - Both tools include data freshness → pass (asserted in `TestCompareSpending` and `TestQueryTransactions_SplitsDeletedAndBoundaries`).
  - Bad input returns a specific client error → pass: `TestQueryTransactions_BadInput`, `TestCompareSpending_BadPeriods`.
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` → pass.
- Deviations from brief: none. Design choices for review: query results are lines, not whole transactions, so a split shows up as several lines with the same `transaction_id`. Amount filters are signed (outflows negative). Spending is reported as positive outflow (`-sum`). An account or category name that doesn't exist is a client error, not an empty result, so "no match" can't be mistaken for "no spending". Transactions in off-budget accounts show up in `query_transactions` but not in `compare_spending`.
- Follow-ups for backlog: `compare_spending` has no averaged multi-period baseline (e.g. "vs my last 3 months' average"); periods of different lengths are only flagged through `days`. Category names match case-insensitively for ASCII only (SQLite `lower`). If a category name exists in two groups, both match.
- Docs follow-ups: CLAUDE.md `store/` role: mention the split-aware read queries (`QueryLines`, `CategoryTotals`) in `store/transactions_read.go`. CLAUDE.md MCP section (once there is one): the tools are `query_transactions` and `compare_spending`; `badRequest` is the way to send a client a specific error.
